page: Amazon Web Services m4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the m4.xlarge in the lower performance tiers compared to newer cloud hardware. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register scores of 1282.39 and 3353.46 respectively, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with uncached read and write bandwidths of 24.01 GB/sec and 21.65 GB/sec. Real-world application benchmarks show a static web serving throughput of 3.36 GB/sec and a Redis SET operations rate of 1.44 million operations per second, which ranks in the bottom 10%.

Given its older hardware generation and lower resource density, the m4.xlarge represents a legacy general-purpose option. It is best suited for low-intensity workloads that require dedicated vCPUs and a balanced memory-to-CPU ratio but do not demand high computational throughput. Suitable applications include basic web serving, lightweight background processing, development environments, and small-scale database operations that do not require high IOPS or local SSD storage.
